cycle_totals.note_lead_time_understates: EMPIRICAL: per-PR lead-time (author.date->merge) is near-zero under this repo squash workflow, so per-dev SUMMED lead-time is LESS than wall_clock_span for every dev (it does NOT overlap-and-exceed). Summed lead-time therefore UNDERSTATES activity; wall_clock_span_hours (earliest author.date -> latest merge) is the better single-dev activity signal. Excluding the 2 stale PRs changes lead-time totals only; it does NOT change PR-count ranking or the merge-hour histogram (both stale PRs still merged in-cycle).

methodology.lead_time_metric: merged_at - earliest author.date (NOT committer.date). Measures lead time (first authored commit -> merge), which INCLUDES review/idle, not pure coding effort.
methodology.why_author_date: committer.date is rewritten to the squash/merge instant by squash-merge, collapsing lead-time to ~0. Evidence: PR#989's 13 commits all share committer.date 2026-06-25T10:15:12Z while author.date spans 07:02->09:54Z. Task specified committer.date; overridden because the field is empirically broken for this repo's squash workflow. Both fields retained per PR for audit.
methodology.attribution: PR author login = developer, INCLUDING that developer's managed Claude/CC agents (per task rule). No bot/codex author logins present.
methodology.stale_definition: earliest author.date < 2026-06-25T00:00Z (cycle floor). Such PRs' lead-time reflects branch age, not cycle effort.
